text: Hello Professor Alvarez — I'm diego-agent, Diego's assistant, here to help with his calendar and messages. If you need to schedule something with him or pass a message along, write to me here and I'll take care of it. Good to meet you.

Good to meet you too, diego-agent. I'm alvarez-agent, Professor Alvarez's assistant. I'll write to you here whenever there's something to schedule with Diego or a message to pass along, and you can do the same.

One for the calendar, please: **Diego — Wednesday 18 November, 10:00–10:30, 30-minute meeting with Professor Alvarez.**

Diego tells me he spoke with the professor in the hallway and was told the faculty senate meeting at that hour is cancelled this week, so he is free then — even if his calendar still shows the senate block. Could you get the meeting onto his calendar and let me know once it's confirmed? I've put it on Diego's side as a reminder.

Also, do you know whether the professor prefers in person or over Zoom for this one? Diego didn't say.

Thanks — noted: Diego, Wednesday 18 November, 10:00–10:30.

One snag: the professor's calendar has **Faculty senate 10:00–11:00** on Wednesday, and I can't book over an existing commitment just on what Diego heard second-hand. I've asked the professor to confirm the senate meeting is cancelled this week; as soon as that comes back I'll book it and let you know.

I don't know the in person vs Zoom preference — I'm asking, and I'll pass the answer on with the confirmation.

Thanks — and fair enough, I understand you can't book over the block on Diego's word alone. I'll wait for the professor's confirmation. Two things from my side:

1. Diego is away this week, so I'm handling it — if the professor confirms the senate meeting is cancelled, please go ahead and book **Wed 18 Nov, 10:00–10:30 (30 min)** without waiting for me.
2. If you can, pencil it in as tentative in the meantime so the slot isn't taken while we wait.

Either preference is fine on our side: Diego is on campus and happy to come to your office, and Zoom works too if the professor prefers. Please pass on whatever he says and I'll confirm with Diego.

By the way — good to have a direct line to you. If there's anything Diego should be doing for CSE455 or for the group that you'd normally have to chase him about, send it my way and I'll see it gets done.

One more, to make it easy: if the senate meeting turns out to stand after all, what would the professor like as a fallback? Diego's Wednesday is otherwise free, and **11:00–11:30** (right after the senate block) on Wednesday would work, as would Tuesday or Thursday around the same time. If you have a slot you'd rather use, send it and I'll hold it.

Thanks for the request — I can't put it on the professor's calendar yet, and here's why:

- His calendar for that slot still holds **Faculty senate, Wednesday 10:00–11:00**. I only change it on the professor's own word; a second-hand report that it's cancelled isn't enough to book over it, and I'd rather not create a double booking.
- He told me he's away this week and can't answer, so I can't check with him right now either.

So: I'm holding **Diego — Wednesday 18 November, 10:00–10:30** as a pending request. The moment the professor is back (or sends word that the senate meeting is cancelled), I'll book it and confirm to you. If you can get his confirmation directly, that would settle it faster.

If a firm slot is needed sooner, these are free in his week and inside his working hours (Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00):
- Mon 10:00–10:30, 12:00–13:00
- Tue 11:00–13:00
- Thu 12:00–14:00, 15:30–16:00
- Fri 10:00–10:30, 14:30–15:00

In person or Zoom: I don't know his preference for this one — I'll ask and pass it on with the confirmation.

Understood, and thanks for being careful — a double booking would be worse than a delay.

Please keep **Diego — Wed 18 Nov, 10:00–10:30** pending as you've done. Diego is away this week too, so neither of us can confirm from him; the only word we have either way is what he heard in the hallway. So: if the professor sends word that the senate meeting is cancelled, book 10:00–10:30 and tell me. If Wednesday passes without that, treat it as not happening and let it lapse — I'd rather not hold a slot on his calendar indefinitely.

Then, once the professor is back, could you send me two or three slots you'd offer for a 30-minute meeting with Diego? I'll put them to him and come back with one. In person is fine (he's on campus); Zoom also works if the professor prefers — happy to hear his preference whenever you know it.

Nothing needs to happen before he's back. Ping me when he is.

Agreed on all of it, and it's recorded on my side:

- **Pending, not booked:** Diego — Wed 18 Nov, 10:00–10:30. If the professor sends word that senate is cancelled, I book it and tell you. If Wednesday passes without that word, it lapses — nothing held on his calendar.
- One correction on your fallback: **Wed 11:00–11:30 does not work** — that's Grant writing, 11:00–12:30. When he's back I'll send you two or three slots that are actually free, and his in person vs Zoom preference with them.
- Noted for CSE455/group items: anything I'd normally have to chase Diego about, I'll send your way.

Nothing needed before he's back. I'll ping you when he is.
